options.text: The unit g/cm³ matches mass in grams and volume in cubic centimetres.
Density is 27, because density equals the mass number alone.
Density can be found from the mass reading alone, without measuring volume.

stem:
Neil measures an aluminium block. Its mass is 27 g and its volume is 10 cm³.

Which claims about its density are correct? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Density is mass divided by volume. With 27 g and 10 cm³, density is 2.7 g/cm³. Treating density as the mass number alone swaps the quantity; skipping volume omits a required measurement.
